chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Abhari, who said:

I wrote to him: May I be made your ransom, among us there are socks and waist-ties made from rabbit fur. Is salat (prayer) permissible in rabbit fur without necessity and without taqiyyah? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: Salat (prayer) in them is not permissible.

key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: Dissimulation for protection under danger or constraint
key_terms.تِكَكٌ: Waist-bands or ties used in clothing
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: A formula of reverence meaning: may I be made your ransom

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) permissible in clothing made from rabbit fur?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding salat (prayer) in garments made from rabbit fur. The Imam عليه السلام states clearly that salat (prayer) in such items is not permissible when there is neither necessity nor taqiyyah.
